content:
**Visual observations on test image:**
- Very young soybean seedlings (~4-6 cm tall) completely collapsed and wilted at soil line
- Sandy soil conditions
- Leaves are drooping/wilted — soft, tan-green collapse
- Multiple plants affected in the same area
- No obvious spots or lesions visible on leaves — pure damping-off/collar rot pattern

**Narrowing candidates:**
- **Pythium_damping_off**: very early seedlings, water-soaked lesions, soil sticking to seeds
- **Rhizoctonia**: reddish-brown stem lesion at soil line, hypocotyl collapse, seedlings bent over
- **Phytophthora**: older plants, chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward

The Pythium reference shows seeds/cotyledon-stage seedlings with soft rot. The Rhizoctonia reference (bottom-right panel) shows exactly this pattern: collapsed seedlings in sandy soil, bent over at the soil line. The test image seedlings are slightly larger than Pythium stage and show the characteristic hypocotyl collapse of Rhizoctonia.

The pattern matches Rhizoctonia root/hypocotyl rot — bent-over, collapsed seedlings with no visible leaf spotting. Pythium is possible but reference images show even earlier-stage (seed/cotyledon) with water-soaked soft rot, while Rhizoctonia reference shows this exact bent-over seedling collapse pattern."}
